verdict.rationale: The DOS publishes plain-language instruction pages for forming a corporation. They explain name availability searches, 60-day name reservations, fees and filing rails, and expedite tiers. They also give conversational guidance on completing the form ("Nothing more needs to be added unless you wish to have a different stock structure…", "You are not required to use this form"), plus phone help for questions. This goes beyond statute text and form numbers, though it reads more as form instructions than a structured step-by-step explainer. Missing for 10: an explicit ordered step-by-step walkthrough of the founder's full task, evidence of comparable plain-language guidance beyond incorporation (e.g., LLCs, post-formation compliance), and independent or hands-on confirmation that non-lawyers find it followable.
